description: One pint holds 2 cups. Convert pints to cups and back, with the table for half pints up to four quarts, and worked examples for berries and cream.

faqs.answer: 2 cups. A pint is half a quart, and a quart is 4 cups, so half of 4 is 2.
faqs.question: How many cups are in a pint?

faqs.answer: 1 cup. Half a pint is 8 fluid ounces, which is exactly 1 US cup.
faqs.question: How many cups are in half a pint?

faqs.answer: For water, nearly. A pint of water weighs about 1.04 pounds. For flour it is about half a pound, and for honey about a pound and a half, because weight depends on density.
faqs.question: Is a pint a pound?

faqs.answer: No. A US pint is 473 ml and 16 fluid ounces. A British pint is 568 ml and 20 imperial fluid ounces, about 20 percent larger.
faqs.question: Is a UK pint the same as a US pint?

faqs.answer: 16 fluid ounces. A pint is 2 cups, and each cup is 8 fluid ounces, so 2 times 8 is 16.
faqs.question: How many fluid ounces are in a pint?

felicityNote: The pint box of berries is the measure. A recipe that says 2 cups of blueberries means one pint box, and I never get the jug out for it.

parts.meaning: The volume in the recipe or on the container, in US pints.

howToSteps.name: Read the pints
howToSteps.text: Find the amount in pints in your recipe or on the container. Halves and whole numbers are the usual amounts.

howToSteps.name: Multiply by 2
howToSteps.text: Pints times 2 gives cups. One pint is 2 cups, two pints is 4 cups, four pints is 8 cups.

howToSteps.name: Count the containers
howToSteps.text: A pint box of berries is 2 cups. A pint tub of ice cream is 2 cups. The container is the measure.

howToSteps.name: Check US or imperial
howToSteps.text: An American pint is 473 ml. A British pint is 568 ml, about 20 percent larger, which is 2.4 US cups.

name: Pints to Cups
title: Pints to Cups: Volume Converter
tutorial: One pint is 2 cups. It is the simplest conversion in the US volume ladder: a pint is half a quart, a quart is 4 cups, so a pint is 2 cups. A pint is also 16 fluid ounces and 473 ml, which makes it the size of the carton in the fridge and the glass at the table.

Pints are the unit on the small containers. Berries come in pint boxes, ice cream comes in pint tubs, cream and half-and-half come in pint cartons. A recipe that calls for a pint of blueberries is asking for 2 cups, which is the whole box, poured straight in.

The saying goes that a pint is a pound the world around, and for water it is nearly true: a pint of water weighs about 1.04 pounds. For anything else it is only a rough guide. A pint of flour weighs about half a pound, and a pint of honey weighs about a pound and a half.

The imperial pint is different: 20 imperial fluid ounces, 568 ml, about 20 percent larger than the US pint of 473 ml. A British recipe that says a pint of milk means 568 ml, which is 2.4 US cups. The difference is enough to matter in a batter.

Pints sit in the middle of the ladder, which makes them the bridge between the small and the large units. Two pints make a quart, four pints make half a gallon, eight pints make a gallon. If a recipe gives pints and your jug is marked in quarts, divide by 2. If it gives pints and your measure is cups, multiply by 2.
